reuse.why: Routes every expected-amount computation (preview, forecast, budget template, action sync, posting, API list and the desktop views) through the existing getScheduledAmount and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance.

duplication.why: Removes five inline copies of the missing/number/range dispatch (shared preview, forecast-schedules, schedule-template, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule) in favour of the one helper.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts; expectedAmount is added in the api/schedules-get handler rather than in scheduleModel.toExternal, which is a defensible but slightly less central spot.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and its consumers; the release notes include ones describing intermediate rules (furthest from zero) that the final behaviour superseded.

maintainability.why: One function with the operator as an explicit argument decides the expected amount everywhere, so future rule changes land in one place.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No call site re-implements the amount rule after the change.

disguised_duplication.where: Existing copies were removed, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount gained the amount operator (the real variation) and an 'isapprox' branch; all inline re-implementations were replaced by calls, and every consumer passes its operator (useScheduleEdit's form-conversion calls omit it, which matches their purpose).
